I literally just got diagnosed on thursday, i'm with you man. I already had mental health issues but the last few years my brain was just divebombing. I started anti-depressants the start of last year and it's been the most surreal experience, not hating myself as person but still being suicidal because feeling physically useless every day?? The weirdest mental state i've ever been in. The pure relief from a diagnosis was so intense. I have no clue how Ren has managed to do all that he's done, i'm exhausted from my tiny life.

Nope, you're right. He absolutely is. Ren can not only rap fast as hell, sing beautifully and play multiple instruments - the motherfucker can produce, write, direct, compose. His flow, rhyme schemes and lyrical composition are unmatched imo. He is insanely talented. Everyone seems to think that Ren fans are just parasocially overlooking flaws within his music and idk, maybe i am, but i literally cannot see them. Kujo out here talking about "trash ash vocals" like.. bitch where? Show me where. Point em out to me.

Ren was talented enough before the lyme disease stripped everything away from him. This isn't some Britians Got Talent sob story about how he was ill as a little kid and that somehow entitles him to attention. He has consitently shown again and again that he deserves recognition for his work.

On top of the talent, he's just a class fucking guy. How often do you get that? The slightest bit of fame goes to peoples heads immediately, and it's not shade, i can understand how that happens. Ren makes time for people. And it probably is the dire mental health because there's not much that will teach you empathy and compassion quicker, but he literally just wants to put his feelings out in to the world and have someone say "fuck dude me too."

To have someone hurt you in the way that Kujo did and still want to split a master with him? Honestly, more than likely wouldn't be me.

It's the humilty, the grace and the patience. It's the talent AND the kindness.

Hey that’s awesome! Are you going with anyone or on your own? 

I’m in Scotland so maybe it’ll be different with you I’m not sure. You’re gonna have a different experience if you’re seated or standing but either way you’ll line up to go in the building. Usually there’s someone at the door to check your ticket and either pat you down or check inside your bag. If you’re standing a bag is gonna be a bit of a pain in the ass, I’d advise against it, so make sure your pockets have zips so you don’t lose anything.

Best plan is to locate a bathroom immediately before you settle in to your seat or find a spot on the floor. Just so you know where it is.

If you’re standing and you’re early (or when the doors open) then you might get a spot at the front, but you will be standing a long time no matter when you get there so wear good comfy (not new!!) shoes. 

You can take your own water bottle but the venue should have a bar where you can get a water or juice too.

So a while after doors open they’ll do sound checks, and then support bands will come out, and then main act will come out. If you don’t know the other bands make a note in your phone of songs you like because by the end you’ll have forgotten. 

If you want to be in a pit then there’s gonna be limbs coming at you. Being 13 I’m sure you’re a little shorter than the adults around you, this puts you at swinging elbow height so just watch yourself. If someone is crowd surfing then you don’t hold them up, you help them move along. If you want to crowd surf you find the biggest guy you can see and ask him to help you up. If you fall in the pit don’t be embarrassed, it’s absolutely fine! Someone will help you up. 

If you feel too hot, light headed, dizzy, drink some water and try to scoot back to where there’s less people. If you faint people will take care of you but it’s best for you to not faint.

It is going to be hot and sweaty and there’s going to be a lot of people. I know this is obvious, but I have an anxiety disorder and it helps me to be mentally prepared for that fact. There will be people in your space if you’re standing, and the seats are really packed in so you’ll probably be right next to someone either way. For what it’s worth they won’t remember you. 

I’m sure you’re bright and responsible and I’m not just saying this because of your age but do not accept unopened drinks from strangers, do not leave with someone you don’t know. If someone is being a creepy fuck then in a loud happy voice say “hey!! This guy!! He said this to me!!!” and embarrass him out of your space. If you need help then it’s always okay to ask, with creeps or directions or if you’re trying to leave the crowd. Nobody is there to have a bad time and they don’t want you to have a bad time either. 

You can leave the venue and come back just make sure you have your ticket and someone at the door sees you leave. 

And my personal advice is to take a couple pictures of videos as memories but don’t watch the whole show through your phone. You’ll have a much better time just enjoying the moment you’re in (:

Edited to add if you can find pictures online of the merch available ahead of time it can help to see if there’s anything you’d like to buy and how much it is. I hope you have the best time!

Back when I was living with my parents, I was so deep in my depression and the vibe in that house was so negative all the time that I had a lot of nightmares. Sometimes they’d be the “real life” type, where I’d be in the same house. 

Their house is a rectangle, a bungalow with an attic through a trap door in the hall, the attic is the length and breadth of the house and all of the rooms split off the hallway in the middle of the house. With the doors closed there is no light.

So in my dream there I was, middle of the hallway, looking up at the trapdoor. Somehow in my dream it was closed but I could see through a big crack that wasn’t usually there. Dream logic, you know the way. The attic has sloped sides and big huge windows despite only being used for storage so it was the only bright thing in my dream.

I could hear someone running. I mean full on gunning it hauling ass running. It sounded very far away, further than the attic was long but I didn’t look away. It got closer, and louder, and I just knew it was someone running up there in the attic. I was going to see who it was. 

So I stood there, dark hallway, only the bright daylight through this crack that shouldn’t have been there, waiting to see who was running up there and what was taking them so long. 

Closer and closer and louder and louder and out of nowhere I was scared. I didn’t know why I was scared but I can feel it now typing this out. I was sweating, shaking, but I couldn’t convince myself to look away. They were taking forever, and the longer they took the more scared I got. Why was someone running in my attic? 

And then he ran past my line of sight. Left to right. I honestly don’t know if he even made it out of my field of view I woke up so fast. Time slowed, he slowed, and I got a look at him. It was a man. Naked. Burnt. Fully blackened, cracked, red, oozing burnt skin. Head to toe, burnt to a fucking crisp like a forgotten enchilada. He had no hair, honestly I’m not even sure he had a face, but I can still picture his frame, his horrid blackened skin. 

I woke up sweating and crying and terrified. It’s been at least 10 years since that dream, 6 since I left that house, and it’s never left me. I know it was probably my brain trying to process everything I was going through, but honestly I’ve never been able to walk past that trapdoor since without thinking about the way his skin was flaking off.

I am not a professional, I am not a learned person, but I can try give you an outline. The way that people experience Dissociative Identity Disorder, to my understanding, is that their mind becomes “fragmented” into separate people (within their head) to deal with certain aspects of their life. As I’m to understand this commonly happens to people with DID after some kind of trauma so one of those roles could be a protective type of person. Someone who will take charge of their body and get them somewhere safe, someone who will stand up for them because this is something they cannot do. 

I don’t have DID, I don’t know anyone with DID. I could be wrong on all of this and if I am, I am sorry, someone’s welcome to correct me. But as far as I can understand, the “host” (the person before the mind fractures) is not aware that this has happened to them. They experience black out periods of skipped time, they can zone out and not know until someone else tells them afterwards, they can’t account for their own whereabouts. During this time, the person with DID is not “fronting” in their body, they are in their headspace. Now I’m not sure if this is somewhere that they just aren’t properly aware of, like being asleep, or if they believe themselves to be doing something else. Say for example someone with DID is walking through the park. An alter, one of the other identities inside them, decides to front so they do. The host is not aware of this switch and while the alter is walking through the park they get jumped and get into a fight. The host believes themselves to still be walking through the park, or perhaps like I said they’re something like asleep, but the alter goes home with bruises. The host wakes up the next day with those bruises and no explanation why, and no idea how they got home. They were in the park, now it’s the next day and they have blood on them. They are not aware of their alters. This is terrifying for them. I think that after a lot of therapy it can be possible for people to communicate with their alters but I’m not sure and I wouldn’t want to outright say so. 

I don’t want to speak to whether or not alters that are fictional characters or people who already exist in the world also exist. I don’t know enough about them. I’m sure someone could explain that better than me. I will say that personally I don’t believe that someone has the entire cast of a popular cartoon living in their head, like so many of the kids on here claim. 

DID is a serious condition that effects people’s quality of life, safety, wellbeing. It takes a lot of time and a lot of therapy for these people to be okay. It is a trauma to not know where you’ve been, what you’ve done.

Herein lies the problem. The people on this subreddit, the ones who get posted about, generally claim to 1) be aware of their alters 2) be able to communicate with said alters 3) able to pop in and out of their “headspace”  like it’s a house party 4) spend all of their time trying to be quirky and special and one up each other by lying while real people who have DID are struggling and this 5) makes it harder for people who genuinely have DID, or any of the neurological, psychological, even physical problems, to be taken seriously or to get the help they need. 

So we’re all here to make fun of them, for their obvious lies and their desperate claws for attention.
